core_meaning.primary_meaning: Aisha (عائشة, ʿĀʾisha) is the feminine active participle of the Arabic verb ʿāsha (“to live”), associated with the root ع ي ش. Its meaning is “living,” “alive” or “one who lives.” The name is also historically associated with Aisha bint Abi Bakr, a wife of the Prophet Muhammad and an important transmitter in Islamic tradition.

faq.q: What does Aisha mean in Arabic?
faq.a: Aisha (عائشة, ʿāʾisha) means “living,” “alive” or “one who lives.”

faq.q: What is the Arabic root of Aisha?
faq.a: It is associated with ع ي ش (ʿ-y-sh), a root connected with life and living.
عائشة is the feminine active participle of عاشَ (ʿāsha), “to live.”

faq.q: Who was Aisha bint Abi Bakr?
faq.a: She was a wife of the Prophet Muhammad and an influential figure in early Islamic history and hadith transmission.

faq.q: Is Aisha named explicitly in the Qur’an?
faq.a: Aisha bint Abi Bakr is not named explicitly in the Qur’an; her historical importance is known through Islamic historical and hadith traditions.

faq.q: What does Aisha mean in Urdu?
faq.a: It is written عائشہ and commonly explained as زندہ or جیتی ہوئی — living or alive.
English guides include “AA-i-sha” and “EYE-sha.” The Arabic form contains sounds that Latin spelling only approximates.

faq.q: Is Aisha a feminine Arabic name?
faq.a: Yes. عائشة is grammatically feminine and is used as a feminine given name.
